title: The Render Slate — delivery wrapper for every executable prompt
completeTableMarkdown:
| Row | Content |
|---|---|
| `Render ID` | Collision-resistant ID of this exact prompt package: `<PROJECT>_<Shot ID>__<platform-model>__<operation>__P<nn>` (token rules below) |
| `Intent` | One director-readable line: shot, action, decisive creative constraint (starts with `Canon: DRAFT — …` when the treatment is not yet approved, rule 13) |
| `Crew choices` | One line: the craft-fillable decisions this prompt makes that the canon did not fix (light direction, lens/FOV, camera height, micro-cues) — the director's veto list (rule 13) |
| `Run in` | Route: platform → access route → project/workspace → surface/tool → model → mode as `id ("UI label")`, followed by the KEY and its receipt state (= rule 16) — never a route without version/snapshot and checked date. Example: `Higgsfield → web UI → project "Lighthouse" → Video → Seedance 2.5 → t2v (UI label unverified — read the live task dropdown) — from reference HF-WEB@2026-09-04 (checked 2026-09-04), not live-checked this session; confirm model/mode/workspace on the live form before Generate` |
| `Settings` | Executable UI values: ratio, resolution, duration, audio, any non-default control. Never repeat a setting inside a VIDEO prompt (no double control). Two documented exceptions: a control the project's A/B proved inert on this model — then that aspect goes into its prompt block and the UI setting stays Auto (platform-ui-workflows §1, blockquote "Do the controls bite?"); and the Higgsfield DoP tool (production-pipeline ch. 16). STILL prompts are different: the canvas/aspect/grid line is composition language for an image model and stays IN the prompt, first (style-control §2 "Layout before subject"), AND is set in the UI — that pairing is not double control |
| `Inputs` | One reference per line, numbered from 1 in slot/upload order: `n. @tag = what it is — its one job` (this row IS rule 5's attachment checklist; on a platform with a persistent library the same names are Elements and need no upload — say so). State whether the anchor goes in as a reference or as a literal start/end frame (rule 1). Mark `🟡 token form unverified — match the upload label before running` when the surface could not be seen (ch. 12b) |
| `Store in` | Known platform project/folder or local destination — omit rather than invent |
| `Handoff` | Only for linked work: extension boundary states, edit source + scope (`edit source …__T2V__P01__TK03`), or a continuity boundary |

title: Selection index: brief → recipe
completeTableMarkdown:
| Project constraint | Favors | Penalizes |
|---|---|---|
| Low reroll budget / tight deadline | Malick (mosaic of short moments), Boyle (montage), Ozu (locked frontal statics), Gilligan (wordless process montage) | Tarkovsky, Lubezki-style oners — long coherent takes mean extension chains + high reroll cost |
| Complex action, crowds, physics risk | Greengrass, UGC, Lynch — absorb or legitimize artifacts; Kurosawa — telephoto crowd planes + weather cover | Fincher, Kubrick — surgical frames expose every flaw |
| Dialogue-heavy | Ozu (frontal singles sidestep reverse-angle continuity), Tarantino, Bergman | Greengrass — verité dialogue coverage burns takes |
| Film lives on face performance | Bergman + Nykvist — spend the PERFORMANCE/reroll budget here | Willis (buried eyes), heavy-silhouette styles |
| High continuity risk (many locations/outfits/characters) | Malick, Lynch — elliptical/dream logic tolerates jumps | Nolan cross-cutting — parallel lines punish continuity errors |
| Stylized/animated format | Miyazaki, Anderson, Pixar → pixar-look.md | Fraser/Willis deep underexposure — clashes with readable-face warmth |

title: Harmony map: which packages combine
completeTableMarkdown:
| Director structure | DoP signature | Why it harmonizes |
|---|---|---|
| Spielberg | Kamiński | Blown godlight + smoke gives the wonder-and-threat grammar its sentiment and its war-memory grit — both extremes in one toolkit |
| Nolan | Hoytema | Monumental sober naturalism scales to IMAX mechanisms without gloss; cool restraint matches engineered structure |
| Villeneuve | Deakins → Fraser | Deakins built the monumental-clarity phase; Fraser's texture-first underexposure carries the later dust-and-dread scale — both serve duration-dread |
| Wong Kar-wai | Doyle | Step-printed neon smear IS the longing; structure and image are inseparable here — adopt them together or not at all |
| Bergman | Nykvist | The face-as-landscape structure needs the face-light standard; nothing decorative survives the chamber |
| Allen lineage | Willis | The amber NY period — master-shot talk in underexposed warm rooms; comedy that trusts darkness |
| Sciamma | Mathon | The gaze structure needs flame-and-dusk honesty; portrait stillness is shared doctrine |
| Malick | Lubezki | Wandering whisper-montage requires a camera that lives in natural light and moves like breath |
| Wenders | Müller | Available-light Americana trust — the seeing-road structure needs a camera that treats neon and dusk as sufficient |
| Gilligan | (Michael Slovis / BCS lineage) | Hard-sun neo-western wides, object-POV wit, and time-lapse punctuation were built WITH the house camera department — the image grammar is part of the recipe; no full second package |
| Kubrick / Tarantino / Fincher / Scorsese / Ridley Scott / Wright / Wachowskis | (house signatures) | Their image grammar is baked into the director recipe itself — no external DoP package needed; adding one dilutes |

title: 2. Composition
completeTableMarkdown:
| Tool | Effect | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| Rule of thirds | Natural, balanced | Default; subject on a power point, gaze into open space |
| Central/symmetric | Formal, controlled, confrontational or comic | Authority, ritual, deadpan; breaks feel deliberate |
| Leading lines | Steers the eye | Reveals, depth, connecting subject↔goal |
| Frame-in-frame | Isolation, voyeurism, entrapment | Doorways, windows, mirrors-as-shape (not reflections) |
| Negative space | Loneliness, insignificance, dread | Small subject vs. big empty area; horror off-screen space |
| Headroom/lead room | Comfort norms | Break them (crowded headroom, no lead room) for unease |
| Depth layering | Immersion, scale | Always name FG/MG/BG (ties into location plates) |
| High vs. low horizon | Sky = fate/freedom; ground = weight/burden | Establishings, emotional wides |
| Balance/imbalance | Stability vs. tension | Tilt/dutch and asymmetry signal "something is wrong" |

| Pan/tilt | Attention shift | Following gaze or subject |
| Dolly in | Rising importance, realization | Emotional intensification (slow) or threat (fast) |
| Dolly out | Abandonment, context reveal, ending | Loss, punchline reveals, closing shots |
| Tracking/lateral | Accompaniment, parallel life | Walk-and-talks, journeys |
| Crane/rise | Overview, transcendence, epilogue | Openings/closings, scale reveals |
| Handheld | Presence, nervousness, documentary truth | Subjectivity, chaos — dose it, don't default |
| Orbit | Inspection, disorientation, iconization | Hero moments, revelations; expensive — earn it |
| Zoom (vs dolly) | Artificial attention, period flavor | 70s look, crash-zoom comedy/doc |

title: 4. Editing
completeTableMarkdown:
| Cut | Function |
|---|---|
| Hard cut on action | Invisible continuity — cut mid-movement, the motion hides the seam |
| Match cut (graphic/motion) | Poetic linkage across space/time; scene transitions |
| Cut on look (eyeline) | Question → answer: face looks, next shot shows what they see (Kuleshov: the pairing CREATES the emotion) |
| J-cut (audio leads) | Pulls forward, smooth scene entry — sound of the next scene starts under the current one |
| L-cut (audio trails) | Reaction room — we watch listeners while the speaker continues |
| Jump cut | Time compression, nervous energy, comedy of repetition |
| Smash cut | Violent contrast (loud→silent, calm→chaos); comedy and shock |
| Cutaway/insert | Detail emphasis, tension objects, hiding continuity errors |
| Cross-cutting | Parallel action = suspense engine; alternate locations, tighten intervals toward collision |
| Ellipsis | Skip the unfilmable/boring; the audience's mind bridges (also the AI rescue tool, renderability) |
| Scene transitions | Sound bridge (audio crosses the cut — the workhorse) · match dissolve (time passing, memory) · hard black (chapter weight) · whip/wipe (playful momentum, period flavor) — pick ONE transition language per film |

title: 24f. Negation & exclusion — a channel decision, not a wording choice
completeTableMarkdown:
| Model class | Exclusion channel that works |
|---|---|
| Diffusion stills (FLUX, SD3.5, Midjourney, Imagen) | Dedicated negative field / `--no` only — bare atomic nouns ("people", "wall"), one concept per entry (compounds get split and over-exclude), NEVER "don't/no X" in the prompt body |
| AR/reasoning stills (GPT Image, Nano Banana) | Short in-prompt exclusions are vendor-endorsed ("no watermark, no extra text") and legitimate — but the positive description still carries the composition; Google's own rule: positive framing first ("empty street", not "no cars") |
| Video models | Ch. 14 negative rule governs (it's consistent with this research): Seedance names unwanted elements in-prompt (official: "omission is not a reliable negative instruction"); Veo/Kling use their negative fields with bare keywords, most critical first; models without a dedicated negative field → rewrite prohibitions as the desired state ("the boy waves his hands", not "can't stay still") |

title: 24g. Edits & locality
completeTableMarkdown:
| Mask type | Platforms | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Hard** (algorithmic clamp: outside-mask content mathematically preserved) | FLUX Fill (binary b/w mask), Imagen/Vertex inpaint (`maskDilation` ~0.01) | Content cannot escape; the mask truly defines region AND size |
| **Soft** (guidance only) | GPT Image `mask` param — official: "entirely prompt-based… may not follow its exact shape"; may repaint globally | Always pair with the full prompt-level preserve list; expect overflow |
| **No pixel mask** | Nano Banana API (semantic masking by prompt only); Seedream (annotation channel: boxes/arrows/coordinates/sketch instead); Higgsfield mask-brush UI over NB Pro (rough mask OK — expand slightly when replacing, widen + regenerate when an edit misses) | Use the platform's native channel; don't assume mask semantics that aren't there |

title: 24h. Quick reference — problem → first move → hard fix
completeTableMarkdown:
| Problem | First move (prompt-level) | Hard fix (channel change) |
|---|---|---|
| Place an element | Zone language early + named scene geometry | Layout sketch → structure map/annotation → composite layers |
| Set an element's size | Object-class word + shot type/lens + ONE relational anchor | Mask drawn at size (hard-mask platform) / sketch-at-size / composite |
| Small object with detail | Detail described at target scale | Crop-zoom-inpaint-paste-back |
| Exact count | One plain number ≤4–5, simple background | Multi-panel / scaffolded adds / crowd sheet |
| Exclude something | Positive replacement in the same slot | Negative field (diffusion) / short exclusion (AR) / accept-and-post fallback |
| Local edit, keep the rest | "Change only X" + repeated preserve list, ≤3 iterations | Hard mask (FLUX Fill/Imagen) or restart from original with combined instruction |
| Keep composition, change content | Reference + role line ("layout and light only") | FLUX Depth/Canny structure lock |
| Layout fights you twice | Reroll seed (diffusion) or switch to AR-class model | Any of the above — but change CHANNEL, not vocabulary (24b item 7) |

title: 2. Red/yellow list (avoid or mitigate)
completeTableMarkdown:
| Element | Failure | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **In-frame text — unified rule** | Text, logos, subtitles, formulas render as scribble or drift between frames | Default: ALL exact on-screen text goes to post-compositing (officially confirmed by the model vendor's guide). Two documented exceptions: (a) **static short text locked via master plate** — content frozen in the reference image + prompt lock "exactly this one line, frozen and identical in every frame" (production-proven, platforms-models ch. 13b); (b) 🟡 MiniMax H3 has an official quoted-text channel (visible text in double quotes, verbatim, untranslated [MM-off]) and renders UI/text comparatively stably — syntax documented, quality practitioner-rated: test before relying. Dynamic/changing text stays red everywhere. |
| Crowds | Clone extras, melting faces in distance | Multi-variant sheet (production-pipeline ch. 3) with extras as silhouette-distinct CLASSES ("heavy brute" / "light scout") — classes, not outfit variants, kill the clone read; crowds to mid/background; small faces stay unreliable even at high res; fog capped at a stated distance ("visibility 20 m") hides background glitches at army scale (less needed at 4K, still works) [H-off, P25] |
| Hands + fine object manipulation | Finger errors, object morphing | Close-ups only as short single-action beats, cut away before the fine work; the handling invariant is written as a POSITIVE LOCKS line in the ch. 12 structure ("ALWAYS by the handle") — there is no separate CRITICAL block |
| Vehicles/wheels/mechanics | Wrong rotation, illogical mechanics | See rescue paths below |
| Long continuous camera moves | Collapse after several moves (proven in 2.5 too) | One move per shot; cuts instead of tours |
| Instrument fingering, precise sports technique | Approximate only | Frame around it; cutaways |
| Physics as hero (glass shattering exactly, complex fluid pours) | Plausible-but-wrong | Describe end state; hide peak behind cut |
| Tiny hero object carrying the beat (a key, a pill, a seed in a hand) | Object morphs, vanishes or changes size between frames; detail vs. size contradiction (ch. 24b) | Cut to an insert as its own short shot at close scale; carry the beat by the character's reaction; object as a prop sheet (production-pipeline ch. 4) |
| Dark, figure-less macro (no scale anchor, no figure, low light) | No scale read, no material read — the model fills with generic texture or invents a subject | Add a scale anchor or a figure (rule 8 on stylized projects), lift a motivated practical, or replace by a still + ellipsis |
| Continuous approach over distance (a walk/drive/flight that must close the gap on camera) | Scale collapses on the way (same class as wide-shot scale, above); the approach stalls or teleports | Two shots: departure state, arrival state — the distance is an ellipsis (manual cut); never one continuous take |
| Cut back onto the same emissive object (lamp, screen, fire) whose state must match frame-exactly | Brightness, colour temperature and shape differ between takes; the object appears "re-lit" | One state per state sheet (production-pipeline ch. 4); the second view inside the same take, or the object kept in one setup (W10 anchor composition); otherwise accept a grade-side match (post-audio-legal ch. 17) |
| **Wide shots** (stylized 3D; photoreal crowd scale too) | Scale and distance break at wide range; a flat camera path at constant height/speed leaves characters as dots (vendor-confirmed on Higgsfield's own short and its Hell Grind rebuild) | Open the take on a close/medium of the character and transition into the wide inside the same generation; positions locked by the previs/clay render, not by the wide (pixar-look §10) |
| Faces that must stay blank (silent passengers, listeners with no beat) | Model animates them anyway — micro-expressions, drift | Hide by design with a motivated occlusion: reflective glass, backlight silhouette, hat brim, distance — copy-ready GLASS block in video-prompting 12e |
| **Mirror/reflection beats** where a reflected face or pose must match the subject frame-exactly | Reflected face/pose diverges from the subject; reflection doubled, missing, or lagging a beat behind | 🟡 (derivation, not yet [PP]-tested) Reflections as texture/light — glass, water, wet street, chrome — stay GREEN on Seedance 2.5 (§1). For a story mirror beat: Seedance 2.5 only, static camera, ONE readable face in frame — either the reflection alone (subject from behind / over the shoulder) or the subject alone with the mirror as shape (film-craft §2 frame-in-frame); never subject and reflection both readable; otherwise split subject and reflection across a cut. |
